# fivenines_proxmox_nodes (Data Source)

The nodes in the Proxmox cluster this instance reports, and which of them the cluster can no longer see.

THESE ROWS ARE NOT THIS INSTANCE'S. Proxmox inventory is CLUSTER-scoped and organization-owned, so every instance reporting a cluster returns the SAME rows with the same ids. Deduplicate on `id` if you read more than one instance in a cluster. An instance whose reporter has aged out returns an EMPTY LIST, not the cluster's last known rows, with `collector.enabled` still true.

`status = "offline"` IS THE CLUSTER'S VIEW of a node, not ours: the surviving nodes cannot see it. That is the signal worth alerting on, and it is distinct from both "the agent stopped reporting" (`stale`) and "we cannot reach the Proxmox API at all" (the `collector` block).

`stale` here is a fixed 10-minute window -- not the organization threshold the guests data source uses.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "fivenines_proxmox_nodes" "all" {
  instance_id = fivenines_instance.pve_reporter.id
}

# status = "offline" is the CLUSTER's view of a node -- the surviving nodes
# cannot see it. That is distinct from "the agent stopped reporting" (stale)
# and from "we cannot reach the Proxmox API at all" (the collector block).
output "offline_nodes" {
  value = [
    for n in data.fivenines_proxmox_nodes.all.proxmox_nodes :
    n.name if n.status == "offline"
  ]
}

# An instance whose Proxmox reporter has aged out returns an empty list with
# collector.enabled still true -- freshness, not configuration.
output "proxmox_last_reported_at" {
  value = data.fivenines_proxmox_nodes.all.collector.last_reported_at
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The instance (host) UUID the rows belong to.

### Optional

- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the node name.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter over a fixed 10-minute window -- what the proxmox_node_status trigger reads, and not the organization threshold the guests data source uses. Omit for both.
- `status` (String) Filter by the cluster's view of the node. One of: `unknown`, `offline`, `online`.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `collector` (Attributes) Why the row list looks the way it does. Read this before treating an empty list as a clean bill of health: `[]` alone cannot distinguish "this host genuinely runs none" from "the collector is switched off" (which deletes the rows) or "this agent is too old to report them". (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--collector))
- `proxmox_nodes` (Attributes List) The rows the collector reported. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--proxmox_nodes))

<a id="nestedatt--collector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `collector`

Read-Only:

- `blocked_reason` (String) The agent's own explanation, where it sent one. Null otherwise.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the operator has this collector switched on for the instance. Switching it off deletes the rows, so `false` fully explains an empty list.
- `last_reported_at` (String) The instance's last agent check-in -- not this collector's. It separates "this collector went quiet" (rows stale, instance reporting) from "the whole agent went quiet" (both). Per-row freshness is each row's `last_synced_at`.
- `name` (String) The collector these rows come from.
- `pending` (Boolean) Enabled, and the agent knows the feature, but the capability is not satisfied yet (missing binary, missing permission). The rows are legitimately absent and may appear on a later tick.
- `supported` (Boolean) Whether this agent can collect these rows -- its own capability verdict where it reports one, its version otherwise. `false` alongside `enabled` means the instance was asked for something it cannot deliver. Read it as "the agent has not said it cannot": the config-driven collectors (haproxy, rabbitmq, php_fpm, wireguard) have no version floor, so an agent predating one still reports `true` with an empty list.
- `unavailable_reason` (String) Why `supported` is false: `host_lacks_feature` (the agent probed and reported it cannot) or `agent_outdated` (the agent predates the release that collects these rows). Null when supported.


<a id="nestedatt--proxmox_nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `proxmox_nodes`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `id` (String) Row identifier.
- `last_synced_at` (String) Server arrival time of the tick that last refreshed this row (never the agent's clock). Null when the row has never synced.
- `name` (String) The PVE node name, which IS that machine's system hostname -- the join key back to an instance.
- `proxmox_cluster_id` (String) The cluster these rows belong to. NOT the instance: Proxmox inventory is cluster-scoped, so every instance reporting this cluster returns the same rows with the same ids. Deduplicate on `id` if you poll more than one.
- `stale` (Boolean) A FIXED 10-minute window, which is what the proxmox_node_status trigger reads -- NOT the organization threshold the guests endpoint uses. See ProxmoxGuest.stale.
- `status` (String) THE CLUSTER'S VIEW of this node, not ours. `offline` means the surviving nodes cannot see it -- the signal worth alerting on, and distinct from both "the agent stopped reporting" (`stale`) and "we cannot reach the Proxmox API at all" (the `collector` block). One of: `unknown`, `offline`, `online`.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
